title: Mirabel and the Vector
premise: Lena Galloway, the fourth clone of a murdered colonial administrator, arrives at dying Kepler Station to close a case no one wants solved and a colony no one remembers. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers her predecessor's murder was the first move in a plot to seize the relay that governs all traffic through dead space. Pursued by the conspirators who made her and haunted by the original's memories bleeding into her own, Lena must decide whether she is a copy of a dead woman or someone new. In the end she reaches the relay, transmits the truth at the cost of her own signal identity, and chooses love with the station's exiled engineer over the duty she was cloned to serve.
about_author: Ulyana Eriksen is a former orbital-mechanics instructor who left academia to write about the people infrastructure forgets. She lives above the Arctic Circle, where the long dark taught her that isolation is a character.

chapters.title: The Fourth Copy
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She docks at Kepler Station, carrying the original's unsolved murder case and a body that remembers dying. The colony is half-abandoned, its air recyclers failing. Emotional beat: alienation—she is greeted as a replacement, not a person.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, a child nearly dies, and every clock on the station disagrees. Lena realizes the anomaly originated near the dead-space relay. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Original's Rooms
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with fragments of the original's recorded logs. She searches her predecessor's sealed quarters and finds encrypted notes about relay ownership and a name: Vashti Okafor, the station's exiled engineer. Beat: intimacy with a dead stranger.

chapters.title: Vashti
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. The engineer who was blamed for the original's murder lives in the decommissioned ring. She is bitter, brilliant, and convinced clones can't be trusted. Lena offers partnership; Vashti offers contempt. Beat: friction kindling something warmer.

chapters.title: Memory Bleed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The original's memories surface unbidden—she relives the murder from inside the victim's eyes. She identifies the killer's silhouette: a Corporate Continuity officer still stationed on Kepler. Beat: terror of losing the boundary of self.

chapters.title: The Company of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lena and Vashti decode the original's notes together and learn the nine-second flicker was a test of a gravity weapon aimed at the relay. The officer, Halden, begins hunting Lena, calling her 'company property.' Beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: What Copies Owe
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Halden offers Lena her freedom and a clean identity if she surrenders the notes—revealing she was grown specifically to retrieve them. Duty versus self. Beat: betrayal, and the first admission that Vashti matters to her.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Vashti's POV. The two steal a gutted tug and run for the relay through debris fields while Halden's ships burn their wake. Vashti finally believes Lena is her own person. Beat: love confessed in the dark between failures.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the relay, Halden triggers a second gravity collapse to bury the evidence and everyone in it. Lena broadcasts the original's murder record and the weapon's schematics to every colony in the system. Beat: climax—sacrifice of her signal identity to become the message.

chapters.title: Lena
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, months later. The system knows the truth; Halden's faction is broken, and Kepler will live. Lena, legally nobody, chooses to stay with Vashti and rebuild the station—named for herself, not her original. Beat: resolution—identity claimed, love kept, duty redefined.
